reason: The cited evidence (E2) directly supports a phonon drag mechanism at high strain rates and a different mechanism at low rates, but it does not support dynamic strain aging as the low-rate mechanism (E3 shows serrations at high rates, not low rates, for the Co-containing alloy) and provides no data on the Co-free variant, leaving key premises about the low-rate mechanism and alloy-specific behavior unsupported.
premises: Dynamic strain aging (solute pinning) dominates at low strain rates, causing serrated flow
Phonon drag dominates at high strain rates, causing a sharp yield strength increase
A strain-rate-induced transition exists between these two mechanisms
The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy behaves similarly to the Co-containing NiCrFeCoMn alloy in this regard
Serration characteristics shift in amplitude/pattern with the mechanism transition
